name: Citizenship by Marriage to a Nigerien Citizen

requirement_groups.name: Standard route (either direction, since the 2014 reform)

requirements.blocker_text: Code de la Nationalite Nigerienne, Article 13: a foreign spouse of a Nigerien citizen may acquire Nigerien nationality 'en optant pour elle dans un delai d'un an' -- by formally opting for it within one year of the marriage. This is not fully automatic: the government retains an opposition window and can refuse on grounds of indignity, lack of assimilation, or marital breakdown (Article 14). Historically this option ran one-way (foreign wife of a Nigerien husband); Loi No. 2014-60 (15 November 2014) reformed the code to let Nigerien women pass nationality to a foreign spouse on equivalent terms -- making this one of the few countries in this dataset with a CONFIRMED, sourced, symmetric marriage-based citizenship mechanism rather than an asymmetric or unresolved one (contrast ml_citizenship_by_marriage.json for Mali, where the equivalent right remains one-way even after that country's own reforms). The specific reformed article number covering the foreign-husband case was not independently confirmed in this build, though the 2014 reform's substance is corroborated by two sources.
requirements.fix_path: Marry a Nigerien citizen and formally opt for Nigerien nationality within one year of the marriage; the government may oppose on limited grounds.

evidence_required.document: Formal declaration/option within 1 year of marriage

sources.title: Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative (NGO-hosted primary legal text) -- Code de la Nationalite Nigerienne, Article 13 (foreign spouse's one-year option) and Article 14 (grounds for government opposition)
Wikipedia -- confirms Loi 2014-60 extended nationality-transmission-by-marriage rights symmetrically to Nigerien women
